meta.title: Anyone on Earth Can Move Here Without a Visa
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note: Norway's geometry in world-atlas's 110m topology extends north to ~80.7 lat / ~31.3 lon, which matches Svalbard's real extent (confirmed via d3.geoBounds), so Svalbard renders correctly under highlight: ["NO"] -- no marker-only workaround needed for the landmass, unlike San Marino/Easter Island.

beats.voText: There's a place on Earth where your passport doesn't matter. Any citizen of any country can move here, work here, and live here, no visa required.
It's Svalbard, a Norwegian archipelago near the North Pole, open to any nationality since a treaty signed back in 1920.
The catch: there's no welfare system for non-Norwegians here, so you need a job and a place to live already lined up before you land.
Around 2,500 people live here, and polar bears in the surrounding region actually outnumber them, so locals carry rifles outside town.
Buried in a mountain nearby is the Global Seed Vault, backup seeds from nearly every country on Earth, built to survive a global catastrophe.
beats.onScreenText: Backup seeds for the whole planet.

beats.voText: No visa, polar bears outnumbering people, and the planet's backup seed supply buried underground. This Arctic archipelago has it all. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
